nbzinbWebster

nbzinbWebster fits negative binomial (NB2) and zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression models with algorithms written from scratch:

  • nbreg(): NB regression by iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) for the coefficients, alternated with Newton–Raphson for log(θ).
  • zinbreg(): ZINB regression by the EM algorithm, with IRLS M-steps (a weighted logistic regression for the zero part and a weighted NB fit for the count part). Standard errors come from the analytic Hessian of the observed-data log-likelihood.

No general-purpose optimizer (optim(), nlm(), glm(), …) is used in the fitting code. The results reproduce MASS::glm.nb() and pscl::zeroinfl(dist = "negbin").

This package is the STA 651 (Fall 2026) final project of Simon Webster.

  • Website: https://webfam564.github.io/nbzinbWebster/
  • Report: PDF (also on the website as the Report article)

Installation 

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("webfam564/nbzinbWebster")

Usage

The bioChemists data (from the pscl package) record the number of articles published by 915 biochemistry PhD students.

library(nbzinbWebster)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

# Negative binomial regression
fit_nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
fit_nb
#> Call:
#> nbreg(formula = art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
#>
#> Coefficients (negative binomial with log link):
#> (Intercept)     femWomen   marMarried         kid5          phd         ment
#>     0.25614     -0.21642      0.15049     -0.17642      0.01527      0.02908
#>
#> Theta: 2.264   Log-likelihood: -1560.96 on 7 df

# Zero-inflated negative binomial regression:
# count covariates before the |, zero-inflation covariates after it
fit_zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
                    data = bioChemists)
summary(fit_zinb)
#> Count model coefficients (negbin with log link):
#>              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
#> (Intercept)  0.404014   0.141715   2.851  0.00436 **
#> femWomen    -0.211906   0.071922  -2.946  0.00322 **
#> marMarried   0.139462   0.081192   1.718  0.08586 .
#> kid5        -0.167624   0.052457  -3.195  0.00140 **
#> phd          0.001963   0.035586   0.055  0.95602
#> ment         0.024393   0.003518   6.934 4.08e-12 ***
#> Log(theta)   1.002910   0.142830   7.022 2.19e-12 ***
#>
#> Zero-inflation model coefficients (binomial with logit link):
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
#> (Intercept)  -0.8067     0.3532  -2.284   0.0224 *
#> ment         -0.6094     0.2458  -2.480   0.0131 *
#>
#> Theta = 2.726  (SE 0.3894)
#> Log-likelihood: -1553.27 on 9 df   AIC: 3124.54
#> EM iterations: 112 (converged)

# The usual S3 methods work
AIC(fit_nb, fit_zinb)
#>          df      AIC
#> fit_nb    7 3135.917
#> fit_zinb  9 3124.542
head(predict(fit_zinb, type = "zero"))   # P(structural zero)

Both fitted objects support print, summary, coef, vcov, logLik, AIC/BIC, fitted, residuals (response and Pearson), nobs and predict (with newdata). For zinbreg, predict() takes type = "response", "count", "zero" or "prob". Tolerances and iteration limits are set with nbreg_control() and zinbreg_control().

Benchmarks and simulation

inst/benchmark/benchmark.R compares the package with MASS::glm.nb() and pscl::zeroinfl() on pscl::bioChemists and AER::NMES1988. inst/benchmark/simulation.R runs a simulation study of zinbreg(). The results are discussed in the report.
